note: FROZEN external run records for the deterministic run-admission harness.
These are the RECORDS ONLY. They say nothing about the verdict — the
harness holds the expected refusal and its expected named reason. Nothing
in here is read from a live Archon, and nothing in here is a re-implementation
of the admission rules: lib/goal.js discoverRun() consumes exactly these
records through the same fetch boundary it uses in production.
Field names mirror the real run row (scripts/mock-archon.mjs / the OP-4R
fixtures): id, conversation_id, parent_conversation_id, parent_platform_id,
codebase_id, working_path, workflow_name, user_message, status, output.
ONE DELIBERATE DEVIATION from this file's own naming convention: every other
child row names its conversation_id after the row (web-child-harness-ok,
-wrongproj, -wrongmsg, ...). The absent-case PAIR -- no-expected-workspace and
wrong-workspace -- instead SHARES one conversation_id (web-child-harness-wspair),
because that pair's entire content is 'the same run bytes judged against two
associations differing only in expectedWorkspacePath'. The harness asserts that
byte-identity directly (the absent-case test's identityOf guard in
test/run-admission-harness.test.mjs). Both rows were originally written
row-named, which FAILED that guard: the pair differed on conversation_id as well
as on the association, so comparing their two outcomes proved less than it
claimed. The row-named convention is right for every other row and wrong for
exactly these two -- do not 'restore' them.

note: The reads BELOW discoverRun, reached only through runGoal() (_run): the
stray-run diagnostic (findConversationRun), the terminal-state poll
(pollRun), and the dispatch-token detail read whose typed outcome decides
what the discovered-none refusal may claim. discoverRun's own boundary
cannot reach them, so they get their own scenario block. Same discipline:
the fixture supplies records and read outcomes; the harness supplies the
verdict.
ONE ROW HERE IS NOT BELOW discoverRun AT ALL: goal-list-body-unreadable
faults a read INSIDE discoverRun's discovery loop. It lives here rather than
at the admission-level boundary because its content is a VERDICT — UNKNOWN,
and the reason absence would be the wrong answer instead — and a verdict only
exists on the goal path: the admission-level rows assert refusal NAMES. It
also needs the dispatch-keyed fault, which that boundary does not key on.
The fault is keyed on the DISPATCH POST, never on a read counter — a counter
would have to know how many reads tasks.js hydration and the pre-dispatch
snapshot happen to make, which is not a stable contract. 'afterDispatchOkReads'
therefore means: reads before the dispatch always answer, then exactly this
many post-dispatch reads answer, then the fault.
ONE ROW HERE IS A CONTROL RATHER THAN A REFUSAL FINDING:
goal-poll-run-not-terminal serves a readable, non-terminal record on every
poll, so its 30 s terminal window is paid in full (RUN_TERMINAL_WINDOW_MS is a
bare const in lib/goal.js and is NOT injectable — the cost is real and is
recorded, not hidden). It pins that a run which WAS read and simply never
finished is a TIMEOUT, an answer about the run, and never an OUTAGE.
TWO ROWS PAY A FULL DISCOVERY WINDOW BY CONSTRUCTION:
goal-list-body-unreadable faults every post-dispatch list read, and
goal-stray-list-body-unreadable answers the first one and faults the rest,
so in both cases no run is ever adopted and discovery can only end by
reaching ADOPTION_DEADLINE_MS (10000 ms in lib/goal.js, also a bare const
and not injectable). And ONE ROW PAYS THE 30 s TERMINAL WINDOW for the same
structural reason: goal-poll-run-not-a-record serves a non-record body on
every poll, so that window cannot close early either. All of it is recorded
here for the same reason — the cost is real, not a number the fixture can
shrink.

capabilities.name: Verify echo
capabilities.description: Deterministic seeded echo verification for running totals

rows.name: goal-find-conversation-unavailable
rows.what: the run list is readable during discovery (an ANSWERED empty absence) but the stray-run diagnostic read then fails — the outage must be recorded, never reported as a workflow mismatch

rows.name: goal-stray-list-body-unreadable
rows.what: THE FORMER GATE GAP, NOW CLOSED — AND THE ROW DID NOT CHANGE TO GO GREEN. The same axis as goal-find-conversation-unavailable — the stray-run diagnostic's read fails — differing in exactly ONE thing: HOW it fails. Discovery's first post-dispatch list read answers {runs: []} (an authoritative absence, so the counter reaches 1), discovery therefore exits 'none' and reaches the stray diagnostic; the STRAY read then answers HTTP 200 with a body that is not a run list. findConversationRun had no body-shape gate at all — `const runs = (lb && lb.runs) || []` — so it collapsed 'no runs key' and 'an empty runs array' into one value and returned status 'none', which its own doc-comment calls 'an ANSWERED absence'. The caller then recorded NOTHING (the 'unavailable' branch is the only one that sets strayDiagnostic) and refused with run-not-found / 'dispatch accepted but no run appeared': an unreadable list reported as an authoritative absence, the collapse defect in its SHAPE form rather than its parse form. The row asserts the CORRECT end state — the same code, verdict and strayDiagnostic the THROW case already produces — which is exactly why it needed no edit when the fix landed: only the missing strayDiagnostic was ever wrong, and the landed predicate (`if (!lb || !Array.isArray(lb.runs)) return { status: 'unavailable', … }`) supplied it while leaving a json() throw and {"runs": []} untouched. It is kept as a pin because reverting that predicate turns it red again

rows.name: goal-list-body-unreadable
rows.what: THE LIST-SURFACE COUNTER PIN, and the goal.js-side counterpart of storefaults' #48 rows: every post-dispatch list read answers HTTP 200 with valid JSON that is NOT a run list, so no read is ever completed. The discovery counter must stay at zero, and at the adoption deadline that is an OUTAGE (`archon-unavailable`, verdict UNKNOWN) — never the ABSENCE the deadline fall-through would otherwise report. Absence is the dangerous answer here: it prescribes a RETRY, and a retry can double-run a workflow that is alive. The body carries no `runs` ARRAY rather than being unparseable, because 'the body parsed' and 'the body is a run list' are different questions and only the second one is a read: the reader's predicate is `Array.isArray(lb.runs)`. The unparseable-body shape reaches the same branch and is covered on the other reader by storefaults' listMode 'garbage'; this row isolates the contract-level predicate, which is one axis. It has NO dispatch-provided runId, so the dispatch-token branch is skipped and discovery polling is the only path — that is what makes it the discovery-list row rather than another detail row

rows.name: goal-poll-run-unavailable
rows.what: the run is adopted, then every terminal-state poll fails — an outage, never a run timeout

run.user_message: task task-9a0b1c2e: verify echo running total seed values

rows.name: goal-poll-run-not-terminal
rows.what: THE OVER-CORRECTION CONTROL for #64, and a positive control rather than a refusal finding: every post-dispatch detail read returns a WELL-FORMED record whose status is 'running', so every read SUCCEEDS and the run simply never finishes. That is an ANSWER about the run — it did not reach a terminal state inside the named window — so it must refuse as run-timeout with verdict FAILED. It exists so that tightening the poll's success predicate (today `parsed` means only 'the body parsed', so a 200 whose body is `null` or `{ok:true}` counts as a successful read and the window can end in run-timeout for a record we never obtained) cannot over-correct: a readable, well-formed, NON-TERMINAL record must still count as a successful read. A predicate that requires a terminal status, or that treats a `running` record as unreadable, turns this row into archon-unavailable/UNKNOWN and it goes red. Deliberately identical to `goal-poll-run-unavailable` in dispatch shape and run identity, differing in exactly two ways that are the POINT of the pair: that row faults the read and this one never does, and its record is terminal while this one never becomes terminal — so the pair separates the READ OUTCOME from the RUN STATE instead of conflating them

run.user_message: task task-9a0b1c32: verify echo running total seed values

rows.name: goal-poll-run-not-a-record
rows.what: THE KNOWN GATE GAP, and the DETAIL-surface counterpart of the list-surface counter pins: the run IS adopted (read #1 is a well-formed record, so dispatch-provided adoption succeeds), and then every terminal-state poll answers HTTP 200 with valid JSON that is not a run record — `{ok:true}`. The poll's success predicate is PARSE-level (`parsed = true` on any successful res.json()), so every one of those reads counts as a success, no status is ever read, and the window closes as run-timeout: 'the run did not reach a terminal state' — a claim about the WORK, sealed FAILED, for a record we never obtained. The expected outcome is the one the DETAIL READER IN THE SAME FILE already produces for this exact body: lib/goal.js fetchRunDetail classifies `{ok:true}` as INVALID, and its comment names that very body ('{ok:true} and {status:…} carry no id and are INVALID here rather than FOUND with a fabricated id'). INVALID maps to evidence-invalid, which is in OUTCOME_UNKNOWN_CODES, so the verdict is UNKNOWN — an outcome we could not establish, not a verdict about the capability. The body is deliberately `{ok:true}` rather than `{run:null}`: both are non-records, but `{run:null}` is the shape boundary's KNOWN RESIDUAL names as the flip hazard, and this row must not walk into it. It is also INVARIANT under the one sub-question still open for #64 (does the poll stop at the first INVALID read, or keep polling and classify at the deadline?): every poll read is a non-record, so there is never a record read to weigh, and both variants classify it evidence-invalid. This is the sibling of goal-stray-list-body-unreadable: same defect class, the other surface, and the one that has NOT been fixed

run.user_message: task task-9a0b1c35: verify echo running total seed values

rows.name: goal-detail-invalid
rows.what: the dispatch names a run id whose detail read is INVALID: the child serves { run: null }, so fetchRunDetail reaches the 'carried no run id' guard. The none-branch must DERIVE evidence-invalid from the typed rejection instead of claiming run-not-found — a run we hold an id for did appear and its record could not be used as evidence, so the outcome is unknown and a retry could double-run a workflow that may be alive

rows.name: goal-detail-unavailable
rows.what: the dispatch names a run id and EVERY post-dispatch detail read returns 500 — an outage, never an absence. `run` is null rather than a record because no read ever succeeds: a populated record would be dead data implying a readable run exists, and it makes the row fail diagnosably — if the fault ever failed to fire, a { run: null } read classifies as INVALID, so the row would report evidence-invalid instead of the expected archon-unavailable and go red loudly
